grants-<keyword>.notes: OPEN TENSION T1 (addendum-3 sec.7, addendum-2 sec.5): this facet scheme's keyword-identity leaves (e.g. grants-deathtouch-board) collide with the b1-Q1 ruling that pure keyword-grant axes are engine-redundant and were killed. The grammar defines the NAMES; whether these leaves are ever populated/scored is an open engine question reserved for schema pass. This walk does NOT resolve T1 -- it only records the facet scheme as ratified vocabulary, per addendum-3's explicit instruction not to silently resolve it.

<delivery>-unblockable-<scope>.cr_anchor: 509.1h (a creature can't be blocked); 702.111a (Menace, contrast case)

facets.note: static = printed 'this creature can't be blocked'; activated = a paid ability grants it; targeted = an instant/ability grants it to another creature
self = the source becomes unblockable; target = another creature is made unblockable

instantiated_members_current_names: rule:grants-unblockable (= activated-unblockable-target, per its own definition text)
rule:grants-unblockable-target (= static-or-triggered-unblockable-target -- delivery not yet disambiguated)
<delivery>-unblockable-<scope>.notes: PROPOSED, NOT RATIFIED. The walk found 4 live axes covering this space under inconsistent names (none lattice-conformant) with corpus hit-count patterns that overlap substantially (see ratification doc sec.2.4 -- grants-unblockable 407 hits, innate-unblockable 373 hits, measured against the SAME 'can't be blocked' phrase family). Before adopting this grammar, Captain must rule whether the 4 existing axes collapse onto these 4 lattice cells 1:1 or whether real semantic differences (e.g. duration, 'as though it had menace' variants) require additional facets. Do not auto-migrate members.
